subject: VM evidence: scan cadence & archival proof for SOC2 intake
messages:
From: Markus Schulz <markus@fingrid.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: VM evidence: scan cadence & archival proof for SOC2 intake

Hi Irene,

We're preparing for our SOC 2 intake and the auditor has asked for concrete evidence around vulnerability management. Can you please provide:  
- A statement of your scan cadence (how often do infra + container scans run; if schedules differ by environment).
- Retention proof for historical scan results for the last 12 months (where are artifacts stored; retention policy).
- A list of CVEs remediated in the last 90 days and proof (ticket id / patch notes / commit links) that fixes were applied.
- Any SLA or attestation you can sign that covers remediation timelines for critical/important CVEs (we typically need clarity on 30/60/90 windows).

If easier, a single zip with an index CSV of scan runs + a short attestation document is fine. We need to hand this to the auditor by EOD Thursday 2026-04-30.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that's faster.

Markus Schulz
Security Manager, FinGrid Systems
markus@fingrid.com
+1 415-555-0199

Attachment: SIG-questionnaire.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Schulz <markus@fingrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VM evidence: scan cadence & archival proof for SOC2 intake

Hi Markus — thanks for the clear list. Below is a consolidated response and I'll attach the artifacts you requested.  

Quick answers up front:  
- Scan cadence: infrastructure (nightly full authenticated scan every 24 hours); container images (per-build image scan + daily registry sweep); runtime agent-based checks (every 15 minutes for detection only). We run separate schedules for prod vs. non-prod; prod gets the nightly authenticated and continuous runtime monitoring.
- Retention: scan results are stored in the secure evidence bucket in GCS (redwood-vm-evidence) with 13-month retention for full reports and 24 months for the scan index CSV; access is logged via Cloud Audit.
- CVE remediation: attached is a patch list (hotfix-patchlist-202603.pdf) showing CVE id, severity, affected component, ticket (JIRA-xxxx), and commit/PR link where applicable. For recent criticals we operate on a 30-day SLA for deployment to prod, 60 days for high, 90 days for medium by default unless compensating controls apply.

Attachments included: scan-index-20260401.csv (index of runs), hotfix-patchlist-202603.pdf.  

Next steps:  
1) Monica (VM lead) is copying an attestation template and will propose signer names.  
2) Karthik — can you confirm the SLA language below matches our contractual posture and, if approved, we will produce an attestation doc for signature:  
   - Critical: remediation (deploy or mitigated) within 30 calendar days of identification.
   - High: 60 calendar days.
   - Medium/Low: 90 calendar days (or scheduled next maintenance window).

Let me know if you want any additional pivot tables from the index (we can produce environment-filtered CSVs).

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
ireene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: scan-index-20260401.csv; hotfix-patchlist-202603.pdf

Subject: Re: VM evidence: scan cadence & archival proof for SOC2 intake

Markus — adding a formal SLA attestation template and suggested signer roster. See notes below.

On Tue, Apr 28, 2026 at 11:12 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers up front: 
> - Scan cadence: infrastructure (nightly full authenticated scan every 24 hours); container images (per-build image scan + daily registry sweep); runtime agent-based checks (every 15 minutes for detection only).
> - Retention: scan results are stored in the secure evidence bucket in GCS (redwood-vm-evidence) with 13-month retention for full reports and 24 months for the scan index CSV.

Supplemental notes from VM team:  
- Evidence provenance: each CSV row in scan-index-20260401.csv has a run_id, scanner version, target CIDR/repo, and sha256 hash of the report stored in GCS. The auditor can validate these hashes against the stored objects.
- Emergency hotpatch process: for critical CVEs we can trigger an accelerated change window with a temporary rollback/feature-flag mitigation; those events are tracked in the 'hotfix' JIRA label and mirrored in the attached hotfix-patchlist.

Attachment: vm-sla-attestation.docx (one-page attestation for signature). If you confirm the SLA language that Irene proposed, I can sign as VM owner and route to Legal if FinGrid needs a countersignature.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Director, Vulnerability Management
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Thanks Irene and Monica — this is very helpful. Two quick follow-ups before we hand to the auditor:  
1) Can you include explicit evidence for CVE-2026-1234 (we track that in our intake checklist) showing the ticket id + commit and the date the fix was deployed to prod? That will close one of their open questions.
2) Please confirm that the scan-index CSV includes a run for each week going back 12 months (our auditor checks sampling across time).

If you can drop a short signed attestation as a PDF (vm-sla-attestation-signed.pdf) and a link to the GCS folder with the indexed objects, we can close this loop on our side. Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll accept the attestation signed by Monica as VM owner if legal countersignature isn't required.

Best,
Markus Schulz
Security Manager, FinGrid Systems
markus@fingrid.com
